title: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term
content: Brazil's 80-year-old left-wing leader President Lula defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in a bitterly contested runoff.

title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
content: Pennsylvania is the worst hit state, with at least 1,338 cases of measles confirmed in 44 counties so far this year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
content: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.

title: Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile
content: Machado announced her arrival on social media, writing "I am here. With you."

title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?
content: Israel is holding a general election this week after years of war. For many Israelis, shaken by the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks and years of war, it is the most consequential in decades.

title: What makes a good spine-tingler? Stephen Graham Jones says it's all in the ending
content: Horror writer Stephen Graham Jones says horror's current moment is powered by more than just fear.

title: This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians
content: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
content: The recent Meta settlement includes a clause banning "cosmetic procedure filters" for teens. But defining what constitutes an extreme makeover isn't easy.

title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
content: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.

title: Independent candidates sense a moment. Some Democrats hope they're right.
content: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.
